fact: Secretary of State Pedro Lopes said Cape Verde has a dedicated start-up law with tax benefits.
Lopes said the government funds around 100 start-ups, two co-founders each receiving six minimum salaries, and a $24 million Morabeza Fund targets youth- and women-led tech start-ups.
The Ministry of Finance (DGCI) deck says startups benefit from financial incentives, skills support and other institutional support provided in Law 70/VIII/2014 of 26 August.

The Ministry of Finance (DGCI) deck says the 2026 State Budget applies a 5% IRPC rate (2.5% for ICT startups and those outside Praia, Sal, Sao Vicente and Boa Vista) to startups for their first five years, with stamp-duty and import-duty relief.

fact: Cabo Verde's UGPE is preparing a programme and strategy to attract and retain international startups, with expressions of interest open until 18 February 2025, under the AfDB-financed Technology Park Phase II project.

Pro-Empresa reports on the Government of Cabo Verde's AfDB co-financed Fundo Morabeza (EUR 24m) that 1,774 MSMEs were funded in 2025 against a target of 600, with EUR 5.42m executed to 31 March 2026; the page presents the fund as boosting startups.
